body.text: Water as found in nature contains impurities that must be controlled or eliminated.
Deaeration strips dissolved gases, filtration removes insoluble solids, and ion exchange replaces undesirable ions with acceptable ones.
Ion exchange devices are commonly called demineralizers. To demineralize is
A cation is an ion with a positive charge, and an anion is an ion with a negative charge. Both resins belong to a group of compounds called polymers,
Resin beads are very small and look like damp, transparent, amber sand. Cross-linked polystyrene is the polymer commonly used.
A mixed-bed demineralizer is a vessel containing a uniform mixture of cation and anion resins.
A resin is usually named by the ion on its active sites, such as hydrogen form or hydroxyl form.

checks.q: What is the normal ratio in a mixed-bed demineralizer?
o: 2 parts cation resin to 3 parts anion resin
checks.x: The ratio is normally 2 parts cation resin to 3 parts anion resin.

checks.q: What does an anion resin exchange?
checks.x: Anion resins exchange negative ions, and cation resins exchange positive ions.

body.text: For cations, Na+ has a higher affinity than H+, and H+ higher than Li+. For anions, Cl- has a higher affinity than OH-.

checks.q: Why does solution flow from top to bottom in a mixed bed?
o: Different resin densities would otherwise separate the resins
checks.x: Because of the different densities of the resins, the flow is from top to bottom.

body.text: Decontamination factor (DF) is
DF = influent concentration, conductivity, or radioactivity / effluent concentration, conductivity, or radioactivity

body.text: H-R + R-OH + Na+ + Cl- → Na-R + R-Cl + H+ + OH-
H-R + R-OH + Ca++ + SO4-- → Ca-R + R-SO4 + H+ + OH-
H+ and OH- ions from the resin mostly combine to form water.

checks.q: What is the result of passing NaCl solution through a mixed bed of hydrogen and hydroxyl resins?
checks.x: Na+ and Cl- are replaced by H+ and OH-, so the NaCl solution becomes pure water.

body.text: Dissolved gases are removed by aeration, deaeration, or scavengers.
In aeration, water is sprayed through a tower or air is blown through it, and
In deaeration, water is stored in vented tanks.
Scavengers such as hydrogen, hydrazine, and morpholine combine with the gas and remove it chemically.
Filtration removes insoluble solids by passing water through a porous filter medium.
Pressure filters are the most widely used, because they can be installed in a pressurized system.

checks.q: Which method heats water to a slow boil to strip dissolved gases?
checks.x: In deaeration, the water is heated to a temperature sufficient for slow boiling to occur.

checks.q: Why is sand not normally used as a filter in nuclear applications?
o: The silicate ion associated with it
checks.x: Sand is not normally used because of the silicate ion, which tends to increase corrosion.

body.text: A hydroxyl form anion resin and a cation resin in a form other than hydrogen can release hydroxyl ions to help control pH.
The first indication of depletion is breakthrough.
Overheated anion resin releases trimethylamine (TMA), and overheated cation resin destroys its exchange capacity and produces an acid.

checks.q: What is channeling in an ion exchanger?
o: A direct flow of water through the resin with poor contact
checks.x: Channeling is a condition in which the resin allows a direct flow of water through the ion exchanger.

checks.q: What is exhaustion of a resin bed?
o: Essentially all the exchange capacity has been used
The first small amount of impurity appears in the effluent
checks.x: Exhaustion indicates that essentially all the exchange capacity of the resin has been used.

checks.q: What is breakthrough in a resin bed?
o: Small amounts of impurity begin to appear in the effluent
checks.x: Breakthrough is the point when small amounts of the impurity begin to appear in the effluent.

facts.q: What are the three reasons for using very pure water in a reactor facility?
facts.a: To minimize corrosion, radiation levels, and fouling of heat transfer surfaces.
The ratio of concentration or activity at the inlet to that at the effluent of an ion exchanger.

facts.q: What is the difference between breakthrough and exhaustion?
facts.a: Breakthrough is when small amounts of impurity first appear in the effluent. Exhaustion is when essentially all exchange capacity has been used.

summary.text: There are three general reasons to treat water for its impurities.
Decontamination factor defines the effectiveness of the ion exchange process.
Dissolved gases are removed by aeration, deaeration, or scavengers.
Suspended solids are removed by mechanical filters.
When impurity concentration is the same before and after the resin, the resin has reached exhaustion.

blend_notes.note: Demineralizers and Ion Exchangers.docx slide 1.39 says breakthrough indicates resin exhaustion. The handbook separates them: breakthrough is the first impurity in the effluent, and exhaustion comes later on p.24. The lesson uses the handbook. Existing item Q255 follows the Word file, so it is not reused here and should be reviewed.
PWR pressurizer venting and PWR steam plant oxygen control on p.18 and p.19 are left off under the Nov 5, 2026 decision. The lesson keeps general aeration, deaeration, and scavengers.

p.29 says a mho is one millionth of a mho, where it means micromho. The NaCl example on p.30 prints 2.2 µmho/cm, but its numbers give about 2.1, so the example is left off. Figure 6 is used twice, on p.16 and p.23.
Most slides are pictures, so the lesson uses only the text they contain. Regeneration slides are not in the handbook objectives and are left off.
